Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa, most of it Sahara desert, with its people living mainly in the south and west along the Niger River, where the capital Niamey stands. The map shows its area from 1945, when it was a French colony.

Before the French, its lands lay on the edges of Kanem-Bornu and the Songhai Empire, and held the Tuareg Sultanate of Aïr at Agadez and Hausa city-states in the south. France conquered it around 1900 and made it a colony within French West Africa in 1922.

It became independent in 1960 under Hamani Diori. Uranium, mined from the 1970s, became the main export. Severe Sahel droughts in the 1970s and 1980s brought famine. Niger has had five military coups, most recently in 2023, when officers removed President Mohamed Bazoum, expelled French troops and drew closer to Russia, together with Mali and Burkina Faso.
